agent_answer.notes: Eleven of the 20 corpus papers report a factual-accuracy metric (fraction/proportion of answers judged factually correct, answer accuracy = proportion answered with correct facts, or fact-level accuracy); the best method in each is listed in the table. The other nine papers (S001, S006, S007, S008, S010, S012, S016, S017, S018) report hallucination metrics (hallucination rate / hallucination frequency / share of answers with unsupported or invented statements), where lower is better, so they do not measure factual accuracy and no 'highest factual accuracy' method applies to them. In S013 the conditions are coded B (vanilla LLM / no retrieval), R (retrieval-augmented) and A1 (RAG with random passages). In S009, S014 and S019 one table cell is written 'see text' and resolved by an accompanying sentence (RAG 46.5% in S009, retrieval-augmented 53.5% in S014, retrieve-then-read 63.4% in S019).

cells.conclusion: Reformulate variant (question reformulated before search) achieves the highest factual accuracy (78.1% of answers judged factually correct on LawFactQA), ahead of the read-evidence variant (57.1%), the skip-reranker variant (55.8%) and the no-document generator (50.5%).
Parametric-only condition B achieves the highest fact-level accuracy (78.3% on LawFactQA), edging out retrieval-augmented condition R (77.4%).
The parametric-only model achieves the highest answer accuracy (59.8% on LawFactQA), 0.9 percentage points above the retrieve-then-read model (58.9%).
The retrieval-augmented model achieves the highest answer accuracy (53.8% on HistoryQuest), ahead of the fine-tuned model (47.6%), RAG without reranking (44.8%) and the closed-book model (40.6%).
The parametric-only model achieves the highest fact-level accuracy (53.8% on NewsTruthQA), 7.3 percentage points above the RAG pipeline (46.5%).
Chain-of-thought prompting achieves the highest fact-level accuracy (71.8% on TriviaCheck), ahead of retrieve-then-read (67.6%), RAG with random passages (58.1%) and the closed-book model (54.3%).
Condition B (vanilla LLM / no retrieval) achieves the highest answer accuracy (47.5% on PopCultureQA), ahead of RAG with random passages A1 (42.5%) and retrieval-augmented R (40.3%).

cells.conclusion: The closed-book model achieves the highest answer accuracy (60.6% on BioClaimQA), 7.1 percentage points above the retrieval-augmented model (53.5%).
The fine-tuned model achieves the highest answer accuracy (69.8% on SciFactBench), ahead of the RAG pipeline (66.1%), the parametric-only model (62.5%) and RAG with random passages (33.2%).
The no-retrieval baseline achieves the highest fact-level accuracy (64.2% on TriviaCheck), 0.8 percentage points above the retrieve-then-read model (63.4%).

The retrieval-augmented model achieves the highest answer accuracy (64.6% on LawFactQA), ahead of the fine-tuned model (55.2%), the no-retrieval baseline (52.3%) and self-consistency decoding (35.7%).
